summary: Read-only review of PR #499 at 561428dd (base fbaa78d8, 2 commits). Nothing from the PR was executed and no tests were run by the reviewer. Design: manual workflow_dispatch only; every job is guarded on repository, refs/heads/main, the fixed workflow_ref, actor == triggering_actor == 'l2v-hub', sha == workflow_sha == inputs.reviewed_sha. The script re-checks all of this and also checks fresh main SHA, admin permission, environment id/name and a main-only custom branch policy. Top-level permissions are contents: read. Actions are pinned by SHA, persist-credentials is false, and the concurrency group is dedicated ('protect-demo-secret-scope', not railway-backend). Credential-free tests run in a preflight job before any secret-bearing job. Secret resolution is handled soundly. In the environment-bound jobs, secrets.RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN resolves to the environment copy when one exists, otherwise to the repository copy. The code writes only when the environment copy is absent, so a stale repo value can never overwrite an existing environment value. The only value written is the one consumers already read through repo fallback. At this SHA every consumer of RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN (deploy-backend, codex-bug-release, configure-demo-source, inspect-demo-source-topology) runs in 'glistening-friendship / demo'. So when the environment copy exists it is already the effective value, and deleting the repo copy cannot change what any consumer receives. That covers the env-only, repo-only, both-equal and both-different cases. Before deleting, the code requires the environment copy to be listed, both in a fresh inventory and after re-checking main, admin and the environment. Delete happens at most once, followed by a readback. An uncertain write or delete fails closed with no delete. Verification is by name only: no value, hash or fingerprint is computed, logged or emitted. The receipt is printed as JSON with no value, errors are printed only as codes, and GitHub masks the secret automatically. The value goes to the child process only on stdin. The child env is allowlisted (PATH, HOME, proxies, CA, GH_TOKEN) and excludes RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN. Crypto is delegated to the runner-preinstalled gh CLI ('gh secret set --env'), which seals the value with the environment public key and key_id. No crypto code is fetched at runtime, but the gh version is the runner image's, not pinned. Org-level secrets: GET users/l2v-hub reports type User, so no org secret scope exists. The bug-pipeline-tests.yml change only appends the credential-free helper test to the existing node --test command. Evidence binding: the sha256 of the shipped workflow, script and test match followup-author-seal.json, and bug-pipeline-tests.yml matches native-ci-seal.json (1d7a3a07...). CI at the SHA: all GitHub checks pass (archive-tests, browser-e2e, bug-pipeline-tests, frontend-tests, gate, real-provider, secret-scan, windows-review-setup). Vercel failed on a free-tier rate limit, which is unrelated. One functional gap remains in the only path that writes, see the finding. It is fail-closed (no delete happens), but the repo-only migration path is never exercised against a real gh CLI or API, and the environment name contains ' / '.

findings.problem: The only write path, used in the repo-only case, which is the very case this PR exists for, runs 'gh secret set RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN --env "glistening-friendship / demo"' through the unpinned gh preinstalled on the runner. gh builds the environment public-key and secret routes by interpolating the environment name into the REST path. Nothing shows that the installed gh URL-escapes a name containing a space and a slash, while this script's own API client deliberately uses encodeURIComponent for the same name. If gh does not escape it, the request goes to /environments/glistening-friendship%20/%20demo/... and fails, or targets a wrong route. The job then stops with ENVIRONMENT_WRITE_UNCERTAIN. That is safe, because nothing is deleted, but the migration can never complete. The only test of the writer uses a fake 'gh' script that records argv, so the encoding, sealed-box and key_id behaviour of the real writer is unverified, and the gh/crypto implementation version is not pinned or recorded.
findings.requested_change: Do one of these. (a) Perform the write through the script's own REST client: GET the environment secrets public-key, then PUT secrets/RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN with encrypted_value and key_id, both on routes using encodeURIComponent(environmentName). Do the sealed-box encryption with a vendored or lockfile-pinned, integrity-checked libsodium/tweetnacl. (b) Keep gh, but pin and verify its version in the job (e.g. assert 'gh --version' against an expected value). Then add evidence, such as a gh source reference for that version or a dry-run against a disposable environment whose name contains ' / ', that it escapes the environment name and uses the matching public key_id.
findings.test_expectation: There is a unit test showing that the write request targets /repos/l2v-hub/ClinicOS/environments/glistening-friendship%20%2F%20demo/secrets/... with the key_id taken from the environment's public-key response. The test also checks that the ciphertext opens with the matching secret key under a fixed test keypair, and that the plaintext never appears in argv, env, stdout or stderr. Alternatively, the job asserts a pinned gh version, with recorded evidence that this version escapes environment names. Existing fail-closed tests continue to pass.
